## 1e07c169ac61

### Source identity and reproduced defects

No actionable in-domain generator defect was reproduced in this bounded audit. Audited version 2.0.0 has generator SHA256 `e343c884bfc5aed2f048c0c4a9492e70602aaf04e6df004cbee35f505b917174`. Live canonical execution reported rule hash `b7275e98009a`, equal to the catalog hash; exact rule-text SHA256 is `6333a069cbf649c17249de4a8aeedf040c294dfe0a34dd0f7ca6c40dd07c49e3`.

The rule keeps the unique color-9 anchor fixed and maps every other nonzero cell `(r,c)` to `(ar+c-ac, ac-r+ar)`, preserving its color and dropping destinations outside the grid. My independent implementation was checked against all three canonical pairs (two train, one canonical test), which the selected validator also accepts.

I generated 31 inputs: seed 17, sample indices 0..4 in each of easy/medium/hard (15 default inputs), followed by all four profiles at each dimension corner 6×6, 6×10, 10×6, 10×10 with foreground_size=8 and difficulty=hard (16 explicit-control inputs). All 31 passed self_check, reconstructed every requested control, and matched actual LIVE canonical Racket outputs exactly. No runtime error or label disagreement occurred. Eight deliberately invalid calls covering wrong integer types, dimension/count bounds, unknown profile and unknown axis raised TypeError/ValueError.

### Reproduced teaching witness

`witness.json` records a small positive counterexample to each previously declared shortcut, with complete input, LIVE output and independently computed rival outputs. This is evidence that the shortcuts are refuted, not a claimed defect.

Replay: seed=17, sample_index=0, difficulty=hard; overrides `{grid_h:6, grid_w:6, foreground_size:8, profile:multicolor_disconnected}`. Exact input dimensions: 6 rows × 6 columns. Exact LIVE output dimensions: 6 rows × 6 columns. Its anchor is `(4,1)`, off the integer center `(3,3)`; eight foreground cells use colors 4, 7 and 8 and are four-disconnected. All eight rotated destinations remain in bounds and the rotation changes the source positions. `self_check` returned `[]`; observe_overrides reconstructed the exact four controls. It belongs to the documented axis cross-product and invariants.

The LIVE output has eight rotated foreground cells plus the fixed anchor. Independently computed `first_color_only` retains only the three color-4 cells; `largest_component_only` retains one cell; `center_pivot` places cells elsewhere. Complete arrays are retained in `witness.json`, and its LIVE output is result index 18 in `racket.json`.

Across the 31 inputs, center_pivot was refuted 31 times, first_color_only 14 times and largest_component_only 14 times. The latter two fit all three canonical pairs, making them legitimate canonical-compatible rivals rather than invented negative controls. For each of the three default five-pair windows, I tested all five query positions against the other four LIVE-labelled demonstrations: 15 rotations, zero declared-rival survivors. This corroborates only those retained windows and rivals.

### Suspicions and limits

No additional canonical-compatible shortcut was demonstrated to survive these tested lessons. The finite corpus, one seed and three declared rivals do not establish universal identifiability or exhaustive coverage of the advertised domain. The 16 corner draws test rectangular/high-count constructive support but do not enumerate every interior cross-product or random layout.

Source inspection confirms that connected foregrounds are sampled within one strict half-plane of the anchor and disconnected foregrounds are isolated cells from one checkerboard parity. These are narrower presentation supports than all geometrically valid inputs. I did not turn those restrictions into a reproducible wrong-rule survivor; they remain coverage limits, not reproduced semantic defects.

### Domain questions

The generator explicitly restricts destinations to remain in bounds, whereas the canonical rule also defines clipping behavior. No clipping case is required by its advertised input manifold, so its absence is not an in-domain defect. Likewise, generated anchors are off-center while self_check accepts centered canonical anchors; that broader validator acceptance is intentional compatibility with the original examples, not evidence of a bad label.

### Commands and evidence

Commands, launch/effective working directories and exit codes are retained in `receipt.json`. Generation probe, LIVE apply and final verification all exited 0. The initial `show --format json` probe exited 2 because that command does not support --format; the corrected `show` exited 0. This failed probe is retained honestly and is unrelated to generator semantics. No full battery or source mutation was performed.

Evidence directory: `checks/audit/1e07c169ac61/`. Reproduction and source-bound observations: `probe.py`, `probe.json`, `input.json`. Actual canonical execution: `racket.json`. Independent comparisons and controls: `analyze.py`, `summary.json`. Small witness: `witness.json`. Command provenance: `receipt.json`.

resolution_reason: No actionable defect found within this bounded source-bound audit. Preserve tested scope and presentation/domain limits; not a universal guarantee or a fresh owner run.
